html:
Tamalipueca is the map's name for the native peoples of what is now Tamaulipas, on Mexico's northeast Gulf coast. Spanish sources call them Tamaulipecos.

They were many small bands of hunter-gatherers, related to the Coahuiltecan peoples further north, living south of the farming Huastec towns. Spain left the region alone for two centuries. From 1748 José de Escandón founded the colony of Nuevo Santander there with settlers and soldiers. Missions, war and disease destroyed the bands within a few generations. See also Tamaulipeco tribes on the modern map.
sum: Tamalipueca is the map's name for the native peoples of what is now Tamaulipas, on Mexico's northeast Gulf coast. Spanish sources call them Tamaulipecos.
